findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified but is commented as public and lacks any restricting configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block), allowing unauthenticated access to potentially sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including customer-master.xlsx) are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing risk of data loss or tampering going undetected especially combined with public access.
This object (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII) is stored in aws_s3_bucket.data which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so financial data objects can be modified or deleted without the ability to recover prior versions.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored operational data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored data science data unencrypted at rest.
